title: The origin must still advertise the TTL the composition-skew window is derived from
untested_rationale: The finding is produced by originCachePolicyFindings() in audits/checks/b2-llms.mjs, which reads the Cache-Control response header of a live CloudFront origin fetch. No pure-function llms.txt body can construct a response header, so rule_class: operational is what the schema requires and it forbids a cases[] block. The coverage lives in audits/__tests__/b2-llms.test.ts instead, which drives the orchestration over injected snapshots across the agreeing header, a drifted max-age, a drifted s-maxage, an absent header, and the site side (which must never fire).
rationale:
THE DERIVATION WAS UNMEASURED. coherencePolicy.maxCompositionSkew is 10 minutes because CloudFront advertises a five-minute origin TTL and two intervals tolerate a cross-key or cross-PoP refresh boundary while still detecting a longer hold. Until atlas decision 0142 step 5.2 that five minutes existed only as a sentence in a comment: validateSnapshot judged cache headers for side === 'site' alone, and fetchSnapshot captured origin.cacheControl without any arm ever reading it. If the producer's infrastructure drifted the origin TTL upward, the reasoning underneath the 10-minute window would break silently and B2 would stay green until observed skew actually exceeded 10 minutes -- the very interval the broken derivation no longer justifies.

SOURCED FROM THE CONTRACT, NEVER RESTATED. The expected value is LLM_FRESHNESS_CONFIG.layers.originComposition.cacheFreshness (300 seconds) from @j0nathan-ll0yd/estate-contracts/llms-assurance, the same pinned contract the thresholds themselves come from, so neither this repo nor the producer holds a second copy of the number and a producer-side change moves this rule with no edit here. Measured live on 2026-09-21: all three origin responses returned Cache-Control: public, max-age=300, s-maxage=300 (decisions/evidence/0142-llms-txt-per-file-review/codex-parallel-review/verification/live-b2-final.log).
policy_note: WARN, NOT FAIL, AND ORIGIN-SIDE ONLY. A drifted origin TTL falsifies the WINDOW'S RATIONALE, not the artifact: the bytes, the structure and the composition stamp can all be correct while the header moves, so reddening the weekly step would convert an infrastructure observation into an artifact alert. It is a catalog finding rather than a coherence finding for the same reason llms-composed-at-wire-skew is -- a LlmsCoherenceFinding carries no severity and runB2Llms reds the step on coherenceFindings.length > 0 unconditionally, so a warn is not expressible there. The rule is scoped to the ORIGIN side because the site plane is required to answer no-store (llms-site-browser-cache-policy and llms-site-cdn-cache-policy already fail it when it does not); applying this rule there would contradict that requirement on every healthy run.
applicability: The origin (CloudFront) side of one llms artifact, on a response that carries a Cache-Control header. A response with no Cache-Control at all is out of scope: failedSnapshot sets the field to null for a transport-dark side, and an absent header is not a drifted one -- the darkness is already reported as an unknown by transportObservation.
expectation: Both the max-age and the s-maxage directives of the origin Cache-Control equal LLM_FRESHNESS_CONFIG.layers.originComposition.cacheFreshness expressed in seconds. The two answer different hops -- max-age is what a browser retains, s-maxage what a shared cache retains -- and the skew derivation assumes both, so a drift in either is named. Emission is PER ARTIFACT on the origin side: three origin responses are examined on a full run, so an account-wide TTL change emits this finding three times. The message quotes the header as served, the contract value, and which directives disagreed.
